q20709.en: The white dashed line in the picture may be crossed.

explain.short: A dashed line is broken into pieces. That means drivers are allowed to cross it when it is safe.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'può essere superata' (may be crossed) is right for a dashed line; only a solid line forbids it.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: you may cross it
lines: Cross it only when it is safe

q20710.en: The white dashed line in the picture divides the carriageway into two lanes.

explain.short: The line in the middle splits the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles) into two lanes, one on each side.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'corsie' (lanes): a centre line always creates lanes, one each side.

sceneParams.caption: One dashed line: two lanes

q20711.en: On two-way roads with two lanes, the white dashed line in the picture divides the two directions of travel.

explain.short: On a two-way road with one lane each way, the centre line separates the traffic going one way from the traffic coming the other way.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'divide i sensi di marcia' (divides the directions): on a two-way road with two lanes, that is its job.

sceneParams.caption: Two-way road: the line separates the directions
lines: The line separates the two directions

q20712.en: The white dashed line in the picture allows you, if you want to overtake, to use the other lane for a short time.

explain.short: Because the line is dashed, you may move into the other lane for a moment to overtake, then go back to your lane.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'momentaneamente' (for a short time): you use the other lane only during the overtake.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: overtake using the other lane
lines: Use the other lane, then go back

keywords.en: to use for a short time

q20713.en: The white dashed line in the picture allows a U-turn, in safe conditions, if the road is two-way.

explain.short: A dashed line may be crossed, so on a two-way road you may turn back (make a U-turn) when it is safe and no sign forbids it.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'in condizioni di sicurezza' (in safe conditions): the U-turn is allowed only when it is safe.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: U-turn allowed when safe

q20714.en: The white dashed line in the picture allows a left turn.

explain.short: To turn left you must cross the centre line. With a dashed line this is allowed.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'svolta a sinistra' (left turn): crossing a dashed line to turn left is fine.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed line: you may cross it to turn left
lines: Left turn = cross the centre line

q20715.en: The white dashed line in the picture allows you to drive straddling it.

explain.short: You may cross a dashed line, but you must not drive along on top of it. You drive inside your lane.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'a cavallo' (straddling, wheels on both sides): crossing is allowed, driving on the line is not.

sceneParams.caption: Never drive on top of a centre line
lines: Drive on top of it: no

q20716.en: The white dashed line in the picture separates the road from a cycle path.

explain.short: The line in the picture is in the middle of the road and divides two lanes. It is not the edge of a cycle path.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'pista ciclabile' (cycle path): the picture shows a centre line, not a cycle path.

sceneParams.caption: It divides lanes, not a cycle path

q20717.en: The white dashed line in the picture is found near all level crossings.

explain.short: A dashed centre line is a normal line on many roads. It has nothing to do with level crossings (railway crossings).
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'tutti i passaggi a livello' (all level crossings): this line is not linked to level crossings.

sceneParams.caption: A normal centre line, not a level crossing mark

q20718.en: The white dashed line in the picture can be replaced by a series of road "studs".

explain.short: The centre line must be painted on the road. Studs (small reflectors called 'chiodi') can be added to help at night, but they do not replace the line.
explain.rule: A white dashed (broken) line in the middle of the road may be crossed: to overtake, turn left or make a U-turn, when it is safe. You must not drive on top of it.
explain.trap: 'sostituita' (replaced): studs can only add to the line, not take its place.

sceneParams.caption: Studs can help, but never replace the line
lines: Studs may add to it, not replace it

q20719.en: Lines along the centre of the carriageway may be crossed if they are broken (dashed).

explain.short: A dashed centre line is broken on purpose: you may cross it when it is safe.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'se discontinue' (if dashed): the type of line decides; dashed = may cross.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed centre line: you may cross it

q20720.en: Lines along the centre of the carriageway may not be crossed if they are solid.

explain.short: A solid (continuous) centre line is a barrier you must not cross.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'se continue' (if solid): solid = do not cross.

sceneParams.caption: Solid centre line: do not cross

q20721.en: The middle line in the picture allows overtaking without crossing it, as long as there is no reason that forbids it.

explain.short: The middle line is solid, so you cannot cross it. But you can still overtake if you fit in your own lane, for example passing a bicycle.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'senza superarla' (without crossing it): the overtake stays in your own lane.

sceneParams.caption: Overtake inside your lane, line not crossed
lines: Solid middle line: do not cross

q20722.en: The double line in the picture may not be crossed, but you may drive straddling it.

explain.short: The double solid line must not be crossed, and you also must never drive on top of it.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'ma si può circolare stando a cavallo' (but you may drive straddling it): this second part is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Never drive on top of the double line
lines: Double solid line: do not cross
Driving on top of it: forbidden

q20723.en: Lines along the centre of the carriageway can be white or light blue.

explain.short: Centre lines are white. Light blue (blue) is used for paid parking spaces, not for centre lines.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'azzurre' (light blue): blue lines mark paid parking, never the centre of the road.

sceneParams.caption: Centre lines are white, not blue

q20724.en: The dashed line in the picture can be replaced with some "studs" or reflectors placed 50 centimetres apart.

explain.short: The centre line must be painted. Studs or reflectors can only be added to it; they cannot replace it.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'sostituita' (replaced) and '50 centimetri': both are made up; studs never replace the line.

sceneParams.caption: The line stays painted; studs only help
lines: Studs or reflectors do not replace it

q20725.en: The middle line in the picture does not allow overtaking in any case.

explain.short: You may not cross the solid line, but you may still overtake while staying in your own lane, for example passing a bicycle.
explain.rule: Centre lines are white. Dashed = you may cross. Solid = you may not cross, but you can still overtake if you stay in your own lane.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in any case): too absolute; overtaking inside your lane is still possible.

sceneParams.caption: Overtaking in your own lane is still allowed
lines: Solid middle line: do not cross

q20726.en: The double solid line in the picture is used to divide the directions of travel on two-way roads.

explain.short: On a two-way road, the double solid line separates the traffic in one direction from the traffic in the other.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'dividere i sensi di marcia' (divide the directions): that is exactly its job.

sceneParams.caption: Double solid line: separates the two directions

q20727.en: The double solid line in the picture may not be crossed.

explain.short: A double solid line is the strongest centre line. You must never cross it.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'non può essere superata' (may not be crossed): correct, solid lines are never crossed.

sceneParams.caption: Double solid line: never cross it

q20728.en: The double solid line in the picture allows overtaking, if permitted, without crossing it.

explain.short: You may not cross the double line, but you may overtake while staying in your own lane, if nothing else forbids it.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'senza superarla' (without crossing it): overtaking is fine if you stay in your lane.

sceneParams.caption: Overtake in your lane, never over the line
lines: Do not cross the double line

q20729.en: The double solid line in the picture does not allow a U-turn.

explain.short: A U-turn would cross the double solid line, and crossing it is forbidden.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'inversione del senso di marcia' (U-turn): it would cross the line, so it is not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Double solid line: no U-turn

q20730.en: The double solid line in the picture does not allow turning left.

explain.short: Turning left means crossing the centre line. Over a double solid line this is forbidden.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'svoltare a sinistra' (turn left): it crosses the line, so it is not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Double solid line: no left turn across it

q20731.en: The double solid line in the picture can be found at the edges of the road, to mark the margins.

explain.short: The double solid line is in the middle of the road between the two directions. The edges of the road are marked with a single line.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'ai bordi della strada' (at the edges): the double line belongs in the middle, not at the edges.

sceneParams.caption: Double line in the middle, not at the edges

keywords.en: at the edges of the road

q20732.en: The double solid line in the picture indicates that you may travel in parallel rows.

explain.short: The double solid line only separates the two directions. It says nothing about driving side by side in parallel rows.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'file parallele' (parallel rows): that comes from lanes in the same direction, not from this line.

sceneParams.caption: It separates directions, nothing about rows

q20733.en: The double solid line in the picture shows the point where drivers must stop because of a STOP sign.

explain.short: The STOP line is a single wide line painted ACROSS the lane. The double solid line runs ALONG the road in the middle.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'si debbono arrestare' (must stop): the stop line goes across the road, not along it.

sceneParams.caption: Stop line goes across; this line goes along

q20734.en: The double solid line in the picture is light blue in paid car parks.

explain.short: The double solid line is white. Blue lines mark the spaces of paid parking, they are not double centre lines.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'azzurro' (light blue): blue is for paid parking spaces, not for this line.

sceneParams.caption: Double centre line is white, not blue

q20735.en: The double solid line in the picture may be crossed.

explain.short: A double solid line must never be crossed: not to overtake, not to turn, not to make a U-turn.
explain.rule: A double solid line divides the two directions. You must never cross it: no overtaking over it, no U-turn, no left turn across it.
explain.trap: 'può essere superata' (may be crossed): wrong, solid lines are never crossed.

sceneParams.caption: Double solid line: never cross it

q20736.en: The guide lines in the picture are curved, broken (dashed) white lines.

explain.short: In the middle of the junction you can see curved white lines made of short dashes. Those are the guide lines.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'curve discontinue ... bianco' (curved, dashed, white): all three words describe the picture correctly.

sceneParams.caption: Guide lines: curved, dashed, white
lines: Curved white lines in the junction

q20737.en: The guide lines in the picture are, as a rule, found where the left turn is made leaving the centre of the junction on our right.

explain.short: In Italy you turn left close to the centre of the junction, passing in front of it, so the centre stays on your right. Guide lines show this path.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule): the guide lines mark the normal left turn, with the centre on your right.

sceneParams.caption: Left turn: centre of the junction on your right
lines: Centre of the junction on your right

q20738.en: The guide lines in the picture must be left on the vehicle's left when turning left.

explain.short: When you turn left, you follow the curve with the guide line on your left side. This keeps you on the right side of the new road.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'alla sinistra del veicolo' (on the vehicle's left): correct for a left turn.

sceneParams.caption: Turning left: guide line on your left
lines: Keep the guide line on your left

q20739.en: The guide lines in the picture help you make the turn correctly, without entering the left-hand road on the wrong side.

explain.short: The guide lines draw a wide enough curve, so you do not cut the corner into the oncoming lane of the road you turn into.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'contro mano' (on the wrong side, against traffic): the lines exist to stop this.

sceneParams.caption: Guide lines stop you cutting the corner
lines: Follow the curve of the guide line
You enter the new road on the right side

q20740.en: The guide lines in the picture must always be left on the vehicle's right when turning right.

explain.short: Guide lines in the middle of the junction are for the left turn. A right turn stays close to the right edge and does not use them.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'sempre ... a destra' (always ... right): the lines are for left turns, not right turns.

sceneParams.caption: Guide lines are for left turns
lines: Right turn: stay close to the right edge

q20741.en: The guide lines in the picture may not be crossed by vehicles going straight on.

explain.short: Guide lines are dashed, so vehicles going straight on may drive over them.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'non possono essere superate' (may not be crossed): wrong, dashed lines may be crossed.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed guide lines: straight-on traffic crosses them
lines: Going straight on: may cross them

q20742.en: The guide lines in the picture mark out a traffic island.

explain.short: A traffic island is a closed area with white oblique stripes. Guide lines are only dashed curves that show the path of a turn.
explain.rule: Guide lines are curved white dashed lines inside a junction. They show the correct path for a left turn: keep them on your left so you do not cut into the wrong side.
explain.trap: 'isola di traffico' (traffic island): that is a striped area, not a dashed curve.

sceneParams.caption: Guide lines show a path, not an island
lines: Guide lines: path for the turn

q20743.en: The direction arrows in the picture are found inside the lanes, before a junction.

explain.short: The picture shows white arrows painted in each lane as you approach a junction.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'prima di un incrocio' (before a junction): that is where these arrows are placed.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows in the lanes, before the junction

q20744.en: The direction arrows in the picture tell drivers which directions are allowed at the junction.

explain.short: Each arrow shows where its lane may go: left, straight on, or straight and right.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'direzioni consentite' (allowed directions): that is the meaning of the arrows.

sceneParams.caption: Each arrow shows the lane's allowed direction
lines: Middle: straight. Right: straight or right

q20745.en: The direction arrows in the picture allow you to move into the lane you choose while the lines are still broken (dashed).

explain.short: Where the lane lines are still dashed, you may change lane and pick the lane with the arrow you need.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'ancora discontinue' (still dashed): while the lines are dashed, changing lane is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed lines: choose your lane now
lines: You may move to the lane you need

q20746.en: The direction arrows in the picture oblige you to follow the direction shown if the lane lines are solid.

explain.short: Once the lane lines are solid, you cannot change lane, so you must go where your lane's arrow points.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'se ... continue' (if solid): solid lines make the arrow compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: Solid lane lines: follow your arrow

q20747.en: The direction arrows in the picture are combined straight-right arrows for lanes meant for those going straight on or right.

explain.short: The right lane has an arrow with two heads: straight and right. Drivers going straight on or turning right use it.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'freccia combinata' (combined arrow): one arrow that allows two directions.

sceneParams.caption: Right lane: straight or right
lines: Right lane: arrow with two heads

q20748.en: The direction arrows in the picture can be completed by words on the road surface showing the place you can reach.

explain.short: Next to the arrows, the name of a town or place can be painted on the road, to help you choose the lane.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'scritte sulla pavimentazione' (words on the road surface): place names may be painted with the arrows.

sceneParams.caption: Place names can be painted next to arrows
lines: Arrow + place name on the road

q20749.en: The direction arrows in the picture show the permitted directions.

explain.short: Each arrow tells you which directions its lane may take at the junction.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'direzioni permesse' (permitted directions): that is what the arrows show.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows: the permitted directions

q20750.en: The direction arrows in the picture oblige you to follow the direction shown, even if the lane lines are broken (dashed).

explain.short: While the lane lines are dashed you may still change lane. The arrow becomes compulsory only where the lines are solid.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'anche se ... discontinue' (even if dashed): wrong, with dashed lines you can still change lane.

sceneParams.caption: Dashed lines: you may still change lane

q20751.en: The direction arrows in the picture indicate that you are near an emergency stopping lane.

explain.short: The arrows show the directions allowed at the junction ahead. They say nothing about an emergency lane.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'sosta d'emergenza' (emergency stop): these arrows are about directions, not emergencies.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows show directions, not an emergency lane

q20752.en: The direction arrows in the picture allow us to change lane if the lines are solid.

explain.short: Solid lane lines may not be crossed, so you cannot change lane there. You must follow your lane's arrow.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'se le strisce sono continue' (if the lines are solid): solid means no lane change.

sceneParams.caption: Solid lane lines: no lane change

q20753.en: The direction arrows in the picture are light blue to show a paid car park.

explain.short: Direction arrows are white. Light blue is used to mark paid parking spaces, not arrows.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'azzurro' (light blue): arrows are white; blue is only for paid parking spaces.

sceneParams.caption: Direction arrows are white

q20754.en: The direction arrows in the picture are yellow on roads where parking is forbidden.

explain.short: Direction arrows are white. A no-parking rule does not change their colour.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'giallo' (yellow): yellow markings are for temporary roadworks or reserved spaces, not for this.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows stay white, also where parking is banned
lines: No-parking roads do not change that

q20755.en: The direction arrows in the picture are blue on motorways.

explain.short: Direction arrows painted on the road are white on every road, motorways too.
explain.rule: White arrows in the lanes before a junction show the allowed directions. Lines still dashed: you may change lane. Lines solid: you must go where your arrow points.
explain.trap: 'blu nelle autostrade' (blue on motorways): motorway signs are green, but road arrows are always white.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows on the road are white, motorways too

q20756.en: The traffic island in the picture shows a stretch of road where vehicles may not drive or park.

explain.short: The striped area between the cars is a traffic island (an area painted with stripes). No vehicle may drive on it or stop on it.
explain.rule: A traffic island made of white oblique stripes is a part of the road where you may not drive or park.
explain.trap: 'vietato al transito ed alla sosta' (no driving and no parking): both are forbidden on the island.

sceneParams.caption: Striped island: no driving, no parking
lines: No driving, no parking on it

q20757.en: The traffic island in the picture is made with white oblique stripes.

explain.short: Look at the picture: the island is a group of white stripes drawn at an angle (oblique).
explain.rule: A traffic island made of white oblique stripes is a part of the road where you may not drive or park.
explain.trap: 'strisce bianche oblique' (white slanted stripes): exactly what the picture shows.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic island: white oblique stripes

q20758.en: The traffic island in the picture shows a part of the road where you may not drive.

explain.short: A traffic island is a no-go area: vehicles must drive around it, not over it.
explain.rule: A traffic island made of white oblique stripes is a part of the road where you may not drive or park.
explain.trap: 'non si può circolare' (you may not drive): correct, you go around the island.

sceneParams.caption: Drive around the island, never over it
lines: Drive around it, not on it

q20759.en: The traffic island in the picture can also be made with light blue cross stripes.

explain.short: Traffic islands are made with white oblique stripes. Light blue is for paid parking, not for islands.
explain.rule: A traffic island made of white oblique stripes is a part of the road where you may not drive or park.
explain.trap: 'azzurre trasversali' (light blue cross stripes): wrong colour; islands are white.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic islands are white, not blue

q20760.en: The traffic island in the picture shows an area where vehicles may park.

explain.short: Parking on a traffic island is forbidden. The island is not a parking area.
explain.rule: A traffic island made of white oblique stripes is a part of the road where you may not drive or park.
explain.trap: 'è possibile la sosta' (parking is possible): wrong, parking there is forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: No parking on a traffic island

q20761.en: The traffic island in the picture shows a part of the carriageway where you may park only for 30 minutes.

explain.short: You may not park on a traffic island at all, not even for a short time.
explain.rule: A traffic island made of white oblique stripes is a part of the road where you may not drive or park.
explain.trap: 'solo per 30 minuti' (only for 30 minutes): made up; parking there is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: No parking on the island, not even 30 minutes
lines: No parking, not even for a short time

q20762.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture is before a bend.

explain.short: Before a bend you cannot see oncoming traffic, so the centre line is solid there and you may not cross it.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'prima di una curva' (before a bend): a typical place for a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: Before a bend: solid line, do not cross
lines: Solid centre line: do not cross

q20763.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture is on the uphill side of a crest.

explain.short: Going up a crest (dosso, the top of a hill) you cannot see what comes from the other side, so the line is solid.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'tratto in salita' (uphill side): there the view is blocked, so the line is solid.

sceneParams.caption: Uphill to a crest: solid line, do not cross
lines: Going up to a crest: poor view
Solid centre line: do not cross

q20764.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture is before a junction.

explain.short: Overtaking near a junction is dangerous, so the centre line becomes solid before it.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'prima di un incrocio' (before a junction): a typical place for a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: Before a junction: solid line, do not cross
lines: Solid centre line: do not cross

q20765.en: The vehicle in the picture may not cross the solid centre line.

explain.short: A solid centre line must never be crossed, by any vehicle.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'non può superare' (may not cross): correct for a solid line.

sceneParams.caption: Solid centre line: do not cross

q20766.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture is, as a rule, found on one-way roads.

explain.short: A centre line that divides two directions belongs on two-way roads. On a one-way road there is no oncoming traffic to separate.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'di norma, su strade a senso unico' (as a rule, on one-way roads): wrong, this line separates two directions.

sceneParams.caption: This line divides two directions: two-way road

q20767.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture is found every time you go past the downhill side of a crest.

explain.short: The solid line is placed where you cannot see: going UP a crest. After the top, going down, the view opens again.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'ogni volta ... in discesa' (every time ... downhill): the solid line is on the uphill side, not downhill.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line on the uphill side, not downhill
lines: Uphill to a crest: solid line
Downhill side: you can see again

q20768.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture is found every time you go past a level crossing.

explain.short: The picture shows no railway. A solid line is placed where the view is poor or near junctions, not after every level crossing.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'ogni volta che si supera un passaggio a livello' (every time you pass a level crossing): made up.

sceneParams.caption: Not linked to every level crossing

q20769.en: For the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the solid centre line in the picture allows a U-turn.

explain.short: A U-turn would cross the solid centre line, and that is forbidden.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'consente l'inversione' (allows a U-turn): wrong, a solid line forbids it.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line: no U-turn

q20770.en: The vehicle in the picture may overtake, even crossing the solid centre line.

explain.short: You may never cross a solid centre line, not even to overtake.
explain.rule: A solid centre line is painted where you cannot see far enough: before a bend, on the uphill side of a crest, before a junction. You must not cross it.
explain.trap: 'anche superando' (even crossing): crossing a solid line is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: No overtaking over a solid line
